look_here_first: Inspect the resinous head, stem surface, and mature cypsela: yellow rays around a disk, serrate leaves clasping the stem, glabrous-to-nearly-glabrous gland-dotted stems, and a pappus with numerous bristles. Do not identify from yellow color alone.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Annual herb with branching flowering stems; inspect base and mature shoots.; Alternate, toothed, sessile-to-clasping leaves; resin dots often visible.; Radiate yellow heads with sticky involucral phyllaries.; Stems largely glabrous apart from resin glands; compare hairiness directly.; Mature fruit with multiple pappus bristles; magnification useful.

lookalikes.differences: Versus G. adenodonta, examine stem hairs (adenodonta noticeably hairy/glandular-hairy; ciliata generally glabrous and gland-dotted) and mature pappus. G. nuda is typically rayless, so check head for rays. G. lanceolata has narrower leaves and perennial habit; use stem and head together. G. squarrosa often has strongly reflexed squarrose phyllaries; its historical var. nuda belongs to G. nuda, not this card.
